By Anthony Fenech
Free Press Sports Writer

The way Jay Allen looks at it, if he had never received a life-changing cancer diagnosis in mid-August, then maybe he would have never realized how lucky he is to have all of these people in his life.

“Sometimes, you pull yourself out of the situation and say, ‘Wow, this is for me?’” Allen said in a phone conversation this week. “Sometimes, I’m just amazed. Cards, letters, financial support, everything.
“You don’t feel guilty, you just feel very humbled that there’s many people that care and love you and are concerned about your well-being.”
After two months of cancer treatments, Allen, the Tigers’ public address announcer who was diagnosed with Stage 4 bile duct cancer, is feeling pretty good, he said.

He’s undergoing chemotherapy — two weeks on, one week off — and is looking forward to a cat scan in a couple weeks: The enzyme numbers in his liver have lowered considerably since treatment began, leaving open the possibility that the liver could be healing itself.
“Maybe God’s doing his thing,” Allen said.
But before his cat scan, Allen’s battle will take center stage at his “crazy cancer journey” benefit in the Grand Rapids area on Nov. 2.
Tickets for the event are still available; $45 for a single ticket, $75 for a couple, $250 to sponsor a half-table of five people, and $500 to sponsor a full table of 10 people.
The evening event at English Hills Terrace in Comstock Park includes dinner, dancing, live and silent auctions and a 50-50 raffle — with proceeds benefiting Allen’s ongoing medical expenses.
Allen, 60, has been receiving donations through a GoFundMe account set up by is niece immediately after the diagnosis on Aug. 13.
To date, the page has received $8,483 of its $50,000 goal.
But, Allen said, “You don’t really know what the goal is. God knows what my needs are, so I’m kind of leaving it up to him. He lays the dollar amounts on people’s hearts.”
Allen worked his first season as PA announcer at Comerica Park in 2019. A benchmark in his battle will be Opening Day next April, when he expects to return to the booth for a second season.
“You still feel responsible for this, but I know I’m not,” he said. “You just have to accept it. But it’s been a blessing beyond words, what I’ve seen from people.
“It’s still a very good world. A lot of loving and caring people in this world.”
